Theme

shine verb

also shining, be bright, give light, gleam, glitter, glisten, the sun is shining, shine on

classical

Cic. Off. 1.51 (Ennius): nihilō minus ipsī lūcet
Tib. 1.1.6: dum meus assiduō lūceat igne focus (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 136

lūceō, lūcēre, lūxī

verb, second conjugation, intransitive · Conjugation on Wiktionary

shine, give light

The plain word for anything that gives light: the sun, the moon, a lamp, a fire, eyes. Impersonal lūcet is “it is getting light, it is day” (Cic. Att. 6.2.10).

Other words

  • fulgeō, fulgēre, fulsī — flash, gleam, glitter

    verb, second conjugation, intransitive · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 2.5: quī nitent unguentīs, quī fulgent purpurā (Lewis & Short); Cic. Tusc. 5.62: fulgentem gladium · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Properly of lightning (impersonal fulget, “it lightens”); then of what flashes or glitters: metal, purple, jewels.

  • niteō, nitēre — shine, gleam; look sleek and glossy

    verb, second conjugation, intransitive · also used · classical · Lucr. 1.9: plācātumque nitet diffūsō lūmine caelum (Lewis & Short); Ov. Tr. 3.10.22; Traupman 135; Traupman 321 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    The shine of what is clear, clean, polished or well kept: a cloudless sky, bronze rubbed bright, a sleek animal; also of people and fields, to look well, to thrive (Lewis & Short).

  • splendeō, splendēre — shine, gleam

    verb, second conjugation, intransitive · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.5.7: jamdūdum splendet focus · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Enn., Verg., Hor.)

    Lewis & Short calls it mostly poetic; Cicero has it once, figuratively: virtūs lūcet in tenebrīs splendetque per sēsē semper (Cic. Sest. 60).

  • illūceō, illūcēre — shine on (with the dative)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 3.4.65 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 136 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    (rare (Lewis & Short))

Examples

  • nihilō minus ipsī lūcet, cum illī accenderit

    his own lamp shines no less when he has lit the other man’sCic. Off. 1.51 (Ennius)

  • cupiēbam etiam nunc plūra garrīre sed lūcet

    I’d like to chatter on, but it’s getting lightCic. Att. 6.2.10

  • jamdūdum splendet focus et tibi munda supellex

    the hearth has been glowing for ages, and the things on the table are clean and ready for youHor. Ep. 1.5.7

  • et nitet indūctō candida barba gelū

    and a white beard shines with a coat of frostOv. Tr. 3.10.22

See also bright, sun, sunshine.
